charts.editorial_rationale: The +88,000 May LFS print and the 6.6% unemployment reading are the single biggest factual development this week. A 12-month line chart anchors the rebound visually: it shows the prior summer's climb to 7.1%, the early-2026 pullback to 6.5%, the April uptick back to 6.9%, and the May reversal to 6.6%. Prose narrates the swing; the visual lets the reader see it.
charts.callout_text: May 2026 unemployment fell to 6.6% from 6.9% in April, the largest single-month decline in the 12-month window. The cross-reference engine links the sectoral pattern (construction +27K, transportation +19K, manufacturing +15K) to 964 active infrastructure projects ($200.04B), 468 transport/transit projects ($34.41B), and 79 manufacturing projects ($69.46B) — 1,511 active projects valued at $303.91B.

charts.editorial_rationale: WTI fell 10.7% from the May 19 baseline of $103.02 to $92/bbl this week, but the editorial story is the distance between the spot price and the $50-$65 Western Canadian heavy oil greenfield breakeven cohort cited in public filings. The chart shows the price floating well above the threshold even after the drop — a spatial relationship that prose only approximates.
charts.callout_text: WTI closed at $92.00/bbl on June 8, down 10.7% from the May 19 baseline of $103.02 but still 41.5% above the $65/bbl upper bound of the Western Canadian heavy oil greenfield breakeven cohort. The cross-reference engine links current pricing to 35 active oil and gas projects ($56.53B) and 164 LNG, pipeline, and natural-gas-keyword projects ($167.51B).

charts.editorial_rationale: USD/CAD reached an 8-week high of 1.3949 on June 7, equivalent to CAD/USD at 0.7169 — the weakest loonie print since mid-April. The 8-week trajectory from late March through May 19 shows the loonie peaking at 0.7351 on May 6 then declining through the BoC April 29 hold and the May U.S. payroll surprise. The visual anchors the policy-differential narrative described in the FX commentary.
charts.callout_text: CAD/USD declined from a 0.7351 peak on May 6 to 0.7264 on May 19 in the cached series, with the WebSearch June 7 print at 0.7169 (USD/CAD 1.3949). The cross-reference engine links the 200 bps BoC-Fed differential and the dollar move to 164 LNG, pipeline and natural-gas projects ($167.51B) carrying USD-denominated revenue streams that gain in CAD terms as the loonie weakens.

charts.editorial_rationale: The Government of Canada 2s10s spread flattened to 58 bps from 70 bps in the prior edition as the long end firmed faster than the short. A two-line chart of 2Y and 10Y yields over 6 months shows the spread compression visually — the lines converging toward the right edge. This is precisely the spatial pattern words approximate but a chart nails.
charts.callout_text: The GoC 2s10s spread narrowed to 58 bps on May 19 from 70 bps in the prior edition, with the 2Y at 3.07% and the 10Y at 3.70%. The cross-reference engine links the 5-year fixed mortgage benchmark to 231 active residential projects ($36.27B), and the 10-year tenor to 164 LNG and natural gas projects ($167.51B) whose financing costs anchor to long-end yields.
